text:
sam (pm): quick sync — I pushed a short PRD fragment for Dedicated Capacity guardrails into Notion. Need final numbers for SLA/throughput/autoscale so we can lock acceptance criteria. pinging eng + sres. TL;DR: defined fallback behavior, basic autoscale params, and a few must-have acceptance tests. please reply with hard numbers or objections by EOD. :eyes:

mia (product): saw it. main ask from customers: predictable p95 latency and a clear degradation story. propose we offer two tiers: Standard (99.9 avail) and Premium (99.95 + tighter latency).

raj (eng): quick reality check: latency depends a lot on seq len + batching. our measurements on A100/GPU show approx p95=220ms for 2k tokens, ~420ms for 4k tokens, and >700ms for 8k without batching. cannot promise 300ms p95 across 8k. suggest we specify windows by seq length.

olivia (eng-sre): agree with raj. also: we need to separate contractual SLA (what we sell) vs operational SLO (internal guardrail). operational SLOs should be stricter so we have buffer before hitting SLA. propose internal SLO: availability 99.97, target SLA: 99.9 for Standard reserved, 99.95 for Premium.

diego (research): one more axis: model variant quality. quantized variants buy latency but may hurt quality. Add acceptance tests that check generation quality on our customer prompt set: for e2e checks require embedding-similarity delta < 2% and a small BLEU/ROUGE delta threshold.

raj (eng): concrete numbers proposal from infra side:
- SLA latency buckets: `seq<=2k: p95 <= 250ms`, `2k<seq<=4k: p95 <= 450ms`, `4k<seq<=8k: p95 <= 750ms`
- Throughput baseline: `per-GPU baseline 120 concurrent streams @ avg 2k seq`, degrade linearly with seq length.
- Availability commitment: Standard 99.9 (contract), internal SLO 99.95.

sam (pm): capturing that. autoscale behavior and cooldowns still open. any objections to conservative cooldowns to avoid flapping?

olivia (eng-sre): propose hysteresis config: quick scale-up to avoid latency spikes, and slower scale-down to avoid oscillation. Also need throttles + graceful degradation rules: when cluster CPU/GPU load > 95% fallback to smaller model variant or queue with friendly error message.

raj (eng): here's a sample autoscale config we can use in PRD (dev-ready snippet):
```
autoscale:
  scale_up_threshold: 0.8          # expand when util > 80%
  scale_down_threshold: 0.4        # shrink when util < 40%
  min_replicas: 2
  max_replicas: 30
  scale_up_delay_sec: 120         # allow short bursts
  scale_down_delay_sec: 600       # cool down before shrinking
  max_scale_rate_per_min: 2       # avoid ramping too fast
```

mia (product): looks reasonable. for customers who want tighter SLAs, we'll expose a higher-commit option with dedicated warm pools and faster scale-up. add a line item that Premium customers can request pinned warm pools.

diego (research): acceptance test ideas:
- perf test: run synthetic load for 30m at target QPS with mixed seq distribution. p95/p99 measured per-tenant.
- quality regression: run 500 prompt eval set comparing canonical model -> variant; fail if similarity drop > 2% or hallucination rate increases > 1% absolute.
- degradation playbook dry-run: simulate 2 node loss and verify fallback policies trigger and SLA delta recorded.

olivia (eng-sre): rollout plan notes: canary 5% traffic for 1h, ramp to 25% for 2h, full release after 24h monitoring. observability must include per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency, error/sec, queue length, GPU util, and token-cost breakdown. Also store evaluation snapshots for any rollout that uses quantized model variants.

sam (pm): action items I captured: 1) adopt raj's latency buckets in PRD; 2) add the autoscale config snippet; 3) add acceptance tests (perf/quality/degradation); 4) add Premium warm-pool option and pricing note; 5) add rollout canary and observability checklist. I'll update the Notion doc & flag legal for SLA language.

raj (eng): small implementation note: warm pools add steady-state cost. we should include an example pricing table in PRD showing cost delta for X warm GPUs per commit.

mia (product): yes please include cost examples. customers always ask for TCO numbers.

infra-bot: created INF-3245: "Dedicated capacity guardrails - acceptance test harness" and INF-3246: "Warm pool pricing examples"

olivia (eng-sre): one last thing — add explicit error budget handling. if error budget burned > 50% in a 30d window we trigger escalation to oncall + reduced commitments on new signups.

sam (pm): good call. adding that to PRD. Thanks everyone — if no bikeshed, I'll push an updated PRD with these numbers in 2hrs and tag this thread. :thumbsup:
